author: sjm41
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
PTN000009552 (PTHR10091)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Fly Galml1 (FBgn0052445), Galml2 (FBgn0030525), Galml3(FBgn0032372), 

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**
erroneous propagation
The proteins encoded by these 3 genes have substitutions in their active site and/or substrate binding sites that predict they won't be catalytically active.  Is it sensible/possible to block the 'aldose 1-epimerase activity' annotation to these 3 genes?

NOTE: I have several issues similar to this one based on our recent publication and analysis (https://www.micropublication.org/journals/biology/micropub-biology-001425). Should I make a separate ticket for each PAINT node affected?
title: PTN000009552 (PTHR10091)

author: marcfeuermann
body:
In such multi-duplication blocs it is almost impossible to spot those by eye. I've blocked the annotation for all 3. 
In this case I would suggest you to submit a single ticket including all PAINT nodes affected. It will be faster and easier for you and for me ;-)
Thanks a lot.
